items.title: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Report
CONSENT CALENDAR

Award Contract No. WW-754, West SOMA, Panhandle, and Inner Sunset Sewer Improvements, to responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Precision Engineering, Inc., in the amount $17,912,054 and with a duration of 480 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and four months), to rehabilitate and replace large diameter sewers and laterals on specified streets within the City and SFPUC MAY 13, 2025 MEETING MINUTES County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the West SOMA Sewer Improvement work for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

Award Contract Nos. PRO.0308.A-D, As-Needed Engineering Design Services to AECOM Technical Services, Inc. and Water Resources Engineering, Joint Venture (AECOM-WRE, JV) (PRO.0308.A); Kennedy/Jenks Consultants and AGS, Joint Venture (KJ-AGS, JV) (PRO.0308.B); Brown and Caldwell and Joe Hill Consulting & Engineering Corporation, Joint Venture (BC-JHCE, JV) (PRO.0308.C); and Stantec Consulting Inc. and SRT Consultants, Inc., Joint Venture (Stantec-SRT, JV) (PRO.0308.D), each for an amount not-to-exceed $4,800,000 and with a duration of five years, to provide as-needed professional engineering design and support services necessary for the design and construction of improvements to various San Francisco Public Utilities Commission facilities

Award Contract Nos. PRO.0282.A-C, As-Needed Security Consulting and Design Services, to Catalyst Consulting Group, Inc. (PRO.0282.A), Arup US, Inc. (PRO.0282.B), Jacobs Engineering Group, Inc. (PRO.0282.C), for an amount not-to- exceed $6,000,000 per contract and with a duration of five years, to supplement SFPUC staff to provide technical expertise in security program/project management, engineering design for security related projects, and security design support during construction for security improvements at various San Francisco Public Utilities Commission facilities

Award Contract No. WW-757R, Laguna, Howard, and Mission Creek Combined Sewer Discharge Improvements, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Pullman SST, Inc., in the amount of $7,296,786, with a duration of 510 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and five months), to rehabilitate six combined sewer discharge structures, located along Laguna Street, Howard Street, Third Street, Fourth Street and Sixth Street, in the City and County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

Award Contract No. WW-727R, Various Locations Sewer Replacement No. 16, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Michael O'Shaughnessy Construction, Inc., in the amount of $8,363,587, and with a duration of 580 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and seven months) to replace/line existing sewers on specified streets in the City and County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the SFPUC MAY 13, 2025 MEETING MINUTES purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

Approve increases of $250,000 to the cost contingency and 50 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. HH-1011, O’Shaughnessy Dam Instream Flow Release Valve Replacement with Sierra Mountain Construction, Inc., for a revised cost limit of $6,806,000, and a revised duration limit of 749 calendar days (approximately two years and one month), for additional costs and schedule impacts related to the installation of two new vent pipes to address unexpected cavitation during high-flow releases, as well as differing site conditions that may arise from rising river level during runoff season, and potential issues with the as-built information
Consider and adopt the proposed Wholesale Water Rates and Charges for Fiscal Year 2025-2026
items.text: Consider and adopt the proposed Wholesale Water Rates and Charges for Fiscal Year 2025-2026, which will become effective for meter readings on or after July 1, 2025. The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission developed the proposed rates and charges in accordance with the terms of the Water Supply Agreement between the City and County of San Francisco and its Wholesale Customers, which the Commission approved on April 28, 2009, by Resolution No. 09-0069, and amended and restated on January 26, 2021, by Resolution No. 21-0009, with subsequent approval by the Wholesale Customers. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that this action is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

items.title: Approve an increase of 212 calendar days to the duration contingency for, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant New Headworks Facility, with Sundt-Walsh Joint Venture
items.text: Approve an increase of 212 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WW-628, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant New Headworks Facility, with Sundt- Walsh Joint Venture (Construction Manager/General Contractor or CM/GC), for a revised duration limit of up to 3,516 consecutive calendar days, with no change to the contract amount of $570,380,175, to complete the remaining contract work, and add new scope to demolish the existing all-weather Headworks (SEP 012), which is no longer needed, as the New Headworks Facility is fully operational

items.title: Award professional services, Sunol Valley Facilities Improvements, to CDM Smith Inc., for an amount not-to-exceed $15,000,000 and with a duration of 10 years
items.text: Award professional services Contract No. PRO.0177, Sunol Valley Facilities Improvements, to CDM Smith Inc., for an amount not-to-exceed $15,000,000 and with a duration of 10 years, to provide planning and engineering design and support services necessary for the design and construction of improvements to various SFPUC facilities in the Sunol Valley, subject to Board of Supervisors approval under Charter Section 9.118

items.title: Approve Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. PRO.0068, Biosolids Digester Facilities Construction Management Staff Augmentation Services, with Arcadis U.S., Inc.
items.text: Approve Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. PRO.0068, Biosolids Digester Facilities Construction Management Staff Augmentation Services, with Arcadis U.S., Inc., increasing the contract amount by $26,500,000 and extending the contract duration by three years and nine months, to reflect the current schedule and budget for the Biosolids Digester Facilities Project and to ensure continued construction management support through the completion of the biosolids digester facilities, for a total not-to-exceed contract amount of $68,500,000 and a contract duration of 10 years and nine months, subject to Board of Supervisors approval under Charter Section 9.118

items.title: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Contract Nos. PRO.0233.A, B, C, and E, and Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0233.D, for As-Needed Construction Management Services, with Avila & Associates Consulting Engineers, Inc.
items.text: Approve Amendments No. 1 to Contract Nos. PRO.0233.A, B, C, and E, and Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0233.D, for As-Needed Construction Management Services, with Avila & Associates Consulting Engineers, Inc. (PRO.0233.A), Environmental & Construction Solutions, Inc. (PRO.0233.B), Townsend Management, Inc. and C M Pros Joint Venture (PRO.0233.C), Mott McDonald Group, Inc. and Dabri, Inc., Joint Venture (PRO.0233.D), and GHD, Inc. and Hollins Consulting, Inc., Joint Venture (PRO.0233.E), increasing each contract by $2,000,000, for a total not- to-exceed amount of $6,000,000 per contract, with no change to the duration, to continue providing as-needed construction management services to support the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission’s ongoing capital improvement programs and associated construction projects as well as other public works projects

items.title: Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. WD-2889, As Needed Water Service Line Replacement with JMB Construction, Inc., increasing the contract amount by $4,263,992 for a revised contract amount of $33,594,227 with no change to the contract duration
items.text: Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. WD-2889, As Needed Water Service Line Replacement with JMB Construction, Inc., increasing the contract amount by $4,263,992 for a revised contract amount of $33,174,191 with no change to the contract duration, to add work scope to include pavement restoration work for water service repairs, new water service installations greater than 2-inches, and custom new services including water main extension work

items.title: Approve the 2025 Amended and Restated Water Supply Agreement between the City and County of San Francisco and Wholesale Customers in Alameda, San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties
items.text: Approve the 2025 Amended and Restated Water Supply Agreement between the City and County of San Francisco and Wholesale Customers in Alameda, San Mateo and Santa Clara Counties, amending the 2021 Amended and Restated Water Supply Agreement to (1) revise Section 3.07 concerning Minimum Annual Purchase Quantities, (2) adjust the Minimum Annual Purchase Quantities listed in Attachment E, (3) modify the Tier 1 Water Shortage Allocation Plan in Attachment H, and (4) make other administrative updates and corrections; and authorize the General Manager to amend the Individual Water Sales Contracts between the City and County of San Francisco and Alameda County Water District and the Cities of Milpitas, Mountain View, and Sunnyvale to reflect those four Wholesale Customers’ respective new Minimum Annual Purchase Quantities. SFPUC MAY 13, 2025 MEETING MINUTES

items.title: Approve the Second Amendment to the Individual Water Sales Contract between the City and County of San Francisco and the City of Redwood City
items.text: Approve the Second Amendment to the Individual Water Sales Contract between the City and County of San Francisco (San Francisco) and the City of Redwood City (Redwood City), to (1) adjust the boundaries of the service area where Redwood City may use or sell water delivered by San Francisco to reflect Redwood City’s agreement to take over water service obligations to 12 SFPUC retail customers located in the Redwood City sphere of influence and (2) modify the terms of Section 3 to address the relationship of that retail customer transfer on the SFPUC’s determination of excess use charges that Redwood City may be required to pay during times of mandatory rationing in a declared water shortage emergency, in accordance with Sections 2.03.D and 3.03.B of the 2021 Amended and Restated Water Supply Agreement
